description: Screenshot compiling roughly two dozen news search results (April 2020) reporting on a U.S. Veterans Affairs hospital study of hydroxychloroquine as a COVID-19 treatment. Headlines from Chicago Tribune, Associated Press, Fox News, NBC News, Forbes, Business Insider, The Boston Globe, The Daily Beast, Yahoo and many other outlets uniformly report the study found no benefit and more deaths from the Trump-touted malaria drug. Red boxes have been drawn around the recurring phrases such as 'more deaths, no benefit' in nearly every headline, apparently to highlight coordinated identical wording across outlets. Thumbnails show pill blister packs, a Plaquenil 200 mg box, and a White House briefing.

Recurring body snippet (near-identical across most results): A malaria drug widely touted by President Donald Trump for treating the new coronavirus showed no benefit in a large analysis of its use in U.S. veterans hospitals. There were more deaths among those given hydroxychloroquine versus standard care, researchers reported. The nationwide study was not a rigorous experiment. But with 368 patients ... Other visible phrases: Coronavirus updates from NBC News. Plaquenil 200 mg. About 28% who were given hydroxychloroquine plus usual care died, versus 11% of those getting routine care alone. About 22% of those getting the drug plus azithromycin died too, but the difference. A study backed the words of Dr. Anthony Fauci showing Hydroxychloroquine showed no benefits to patients with coronavirus.
flags: FLAGGED FOR MANUAL REVIEW: compilation of ~23 news-result snippets; all headlines and outlets transcribed verbatim, but the near-identical per-outlet body snippets are condensed to one representative passage rather than transcribed individually.
The red boxes are annotations added by the compiler, apparently to imply coordinated identical media wording; that implication is the poster's claim, not established fact.

description: The official 8chan logo on a white background: a green figure-eight / infinity symbol whose ends taper into leaf- or tendril-like points, with the word 'chan' in black lowercase sans-serif to the lower right, together reading '8chan'. 8chan was the imageboard where Q posts were made from late 2017 until August 2019.

description: Digital wallpaper-style artwork of the Punisher skull logo (from the Marvel Comics character) rendered as a black textured skull with elongated teeth against a red blood-splatter glow on a black background. The Punisher skull was widely adopted in QAnon imagery; the filename 'The_Time_is_Coming.jpg' echoes that use. No text in the image.

Meme pairing a block of text with a photograph of Tanzanian President John Magufuli laughing among officials at a formal event; the laughing man at right edge is consistent with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa. The text recounts Magufuli's May 2020 claim that Tanzanian officials secretly submitted non-human samples (a goat, a pawpaw fruit) under human names to coronavirus testing and that they came back positive, quoting him saying 'Something is happening.' Magufuli did make this claim publicly; the validity of the purported test results was never independently verified.
text: President of Tanzania John Magufuli has outsmarted somebody. He allowed coronavirus testing kits to be imported into his country. He instructed that they be checked by Tanzanian security officials. They tested non-human samples, including a goat and a pawpaw (fruit). The tests were given human names and ages as they were sent off for results. They tested positive. A fruit. A goat. President Magufuli said, "Something is happening."
flags: The goat/pawpaw positive-test story is Magufuli's own claim as relayed by the meme; the samples and results were never independently verified.
Man at right resembles Cyril Ramaphosa but is not named in the image; identification not certain. Other people in the photo left unidentified.
